display.name: Notion
display.blurb: Search the workspace, read and edit pages, query and update databases, manage blocks and comments — authenticated with an internal integration token brokered at the egress proxy.

cli.doc:
Use `notion` to drive the Notion REST API from this session — search the workspace, read/write pages, query/update databases, manage blocks and comments. Authentication is automatic: the egress proxy injects the internal integration token (Bearer) on requests to api.notion.com; `NOTION_TOKEN` is a managed placeholder. The CLI also sends the required `Notion-Version: 2026-03-11` header itself (not a secret). Do NOT set a real token or log in. A page/database/block only responds if it has been shared with the integration.

Subcommands and the power each needs:
- `notion whoami` — the integration's bot user (GET /v1/users/me). Always available.
- `notion search [query] [field=value ...]` — search pages/databases by title (POST /v1/search). Needs `search:read`.
- `notion page <page-id>` — retrieve a page (GET). Needs `pages:read`.
- `notion create-page parent_page_id=<id> [field=value ...]` — create a page (POST /v1/pages). Needs `pages:write`.
- `notion update-page <page-id> [field=value ...]` — update page properties (PATCH). Needs `pages:write`.
- `notion db <database-id>` — retrieve a database schema (GET). Needs `databases:read`.
- `notion query <database-id> [field=value ...]` — query a database (POST /v1/databases/<id>/query). Needs `databases:read`.
- `notion update-db <database-id> [field=value ...]` — update a database (PATCH). Needs `databases:write`.
- `notion block <block-id>` — retrieve a block (GET). Needs `blocks:read`.
- `notion children <block-id>` — list a block's children (GET /v1/blocks/<id>/children). Needs `blocks:read`.
- `notion append <block-id> <json>` — append child blocks (PATCH /v1/blocks/<id>/children); <json> is the request body, e.g. '{"children":[...]}'. Needs `blocks:write`.
- `notion comments <block-or-page-id>` — list comments (GET /v1/comments?block_id=<id>). Needs `comments:read`.
- `notion comment <json>` — create a comment (POST /v1/comments); <json> is the body. Needs `comments:write`.
- `notion users` — list workspace users (GET /v1/users). Needs `users:read`.

Generic escape hatches (any path under /v1, version header added for you):
- `notion get <path> [field=value ...]` — GET, e.g. `notion get /v1/pages/<id>`.
- `notion api <METHOD> <path> [json-body]` — raw call, e.g. `notion api POST /v1/search '{"query":"roadmap"}'`.
Responses are JSON; a 401/403 means the credential or the integration's page-share is missing, a 400 usually means a malformed body.
